title: Normalized degree-zero internal Hom comparison data and their scalar-localized images
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal C)$ for its module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and use integer cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Define $S(F)=F[0]$ by the degree-zero single-complex functor, and let $R_{\mathrm{mod}}$ be the regular module sheaf of $R$. Using the product internal Hom complex $H(L,M)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(L,M)$ and its contravariant/covariant bifunctor [def-pur-hom-complex], put
$$B(F)=S(\mathcal Hom_R(F,R_{\mathrm{mod}})),\qquad T_I(F)=H(S(F),I).$$
For a module map $f:F\to G$, define $B(f):B(G)\to B(F)$ by the single of precomposition with $f$, and $T_I(f):T_I(G)\to T_I(F)$ by the first-variable map of $H$. For $p+n=q$, let $\pi_{L,M}^{n,p,q}:H(L,M)^n\to\mathcal Hom_R(L^p,M^q)$ be the chosen product projection of the already fixed Hom complex. Define $\pi_F^0=\pi_{S(F),S(R_{\mathrm{mod}})}^{0,0,0}$. Let $\sigma_F:S(F)^0\xrightarrow\sim F$ be the canonical single-complex identification. A family $e_F:B(F)\xrightarrow\sim T_{S(R_{\mathrm{mod}})}(F)$ is called normalized if, for every $F$,
$$\pi_F^0\circ e_F^0=\mathcal Hom_R(\sigma_F,\sigma_{R_{\mathrm{mod}}}^{-1})\circ\sigma_{\mathcal Hom_R(F,R_{\mathrm{mod}})}.$$
For any complex $I$ and chain map $j:S(R_{\mathrm{mod}})\to I$, define
$$c_{e,j,F}=H(1_{S(F)},j)\circ e_F:B(F)\to T_I(F).$$
This definition applies to any such family $e$; normalization is a separately defined predicate, not an existence or invertibility assertion about $c$. Finally, for a commutative ring $A$, a ring homomorphism $a:A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$, and $t\in A$, use the induced coefficient action [def-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-coefficient-actions], the derived category $D(\mathcal M)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Define $\operatorname{locObj}(K)=Q_t(QK)$ for every complex $K$, and $\operatorname{locMap}(f)=1\otimes Q(f)$ for every chain map $f$, where $Q$ is derived localization and localized Hom modules are $A[1/t]\otimes_A\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal M)}(-,-)$. No projectivity, boundedness, K-injectivity or quasi-isomorphism is required to define these data.
